title: Automated, Assistive, Non-Contact Sleep Quality Monitor for Older Adults
official: Automated, Assistive, Non-Contact Sleep Quality Monitor for Older Adults
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effect of access to Luna device sleep system data on clinician documentation of sleep disorders and sleep treatments and participants' sleep quality. Participants who have sleep quality measured are long-term care (LTC) facility residents. The primary outcome of the trial is the following:

-Documentation of diagnosis or evidence of treatment of sleep disorders in the electronic health record (EHR) in long-term care (LTC) facility residents after 4 weeks of sleep monitoring and 2 weeks of clinical teams' receipt of resident sleep data. We hypothesize that, when real-time System Sleep Data is shared with the clinical team, i.e., LTC staff and healthcare providers in the facility, sleep disturbances will be more readily detected, leading to timelier, better tailored treatment interventions for sleep disturbances, thereby improving sleep quality.

All participating residents will:

* Have the sleep radar sensor installed for 4 weeks to monitor sleep quality data.
* Complete pre-intervention and post-intervention surveys that will include measures of sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale) and attitudes toward technology, technology acceptance, usability and utility.

Additionally, interviews and surveys will be done with LTC staff and healthcare providers in order to seek feedback and reflections on system use and the sleep data clinician user interface.

interventions.name: Luna Non-Contact Sleep Quality Monitor System

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

For the main outcomes:

-Resident of long-term care (LTC) facility study site location for a minimum of 30 days.

For the interviews and surveys conducted with LTC staff and healthcare providers:

* Provided direct care to one or more participating residents during the resident(s)' participation in the main outcomes of the study and had access to sleep monitoring data for the resident during the study period
* Clinical staff identified by LTC leadership

Exclusion Criteria

For the main outcomes:

-Currently on hospice

For the interviews and surveys conducted with LTC staff and healthcare providers:

-Did not provide direct care to one or more participating residents during the resident(s)' participation in the main outcomes of the study
